title: Distinct permutation dot products
summary: We show that for any two sets of reals numbers $A=\{a_1,\dots,a_n\}$ and $B=\{b_1,\dots,b_n\}$, the sums of the form $\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\,b_{π(i)}$ always take on $Ω(n^{3})$ distinct values, as we range over all permutations $π\in S_n$. An important ingredient is a ``supportive'' version of Halász's anticoncentration theorem from Littlewood-Offord theory, which may be of independent interest.
